name: dante
desc: SOCKS server and client, implementing RFC 1928 and related standards
why: A SOCKS server implementing RFC 1928 offers a door into how proxy handshakes and address negotiation actually work on the wire.

brief.what_it_is: Dante is a SOCKS server and SOCKS client, implementing RFC 1928 and related standards, from Inferno Nettverk A/S. The server sits between internal clients and external hosts, accepting SOCKS connection requests and making the outbound connections itself, so the two sides never talk to each other directly. The homepage says that once installed, Dante can in most cases be made transparent to clients, acting somewhat like a non-transparent Layer 4 router. The homepage does not document specific input or output formats, and it shows no command lines.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames Dante as a way for organizations to control and monitor access in and out of their network, with security through TCP/IP termination (no direct contact between inside and outside hosts), resource control (bandwidth, sessions), and logging (host information, data transferred). It also says it works with many applications that already have SOCKS support built in, such as most web browsers, instant messaging programs, and Bloomberg terminals.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes the mechanism only at a high level: the server terminates TCP/IP on behalf of clients, so inside and outside hosts never connect directly, and it can enforce limits and log transfers at that point. The docs index lists the SOCKS4, SOCKS4A, and SOCKS5 specs (RFC 1928 for SOCKS5, RFC 1929 for username/password auth, RFC 1961 for GSS-API auth) and a set of related IETF drafts, but I did not open those or the configuration pages, so I cannot say how Dante implements them.
brief.install_notes: The homepage does not describe installation steps. It points to configuration pages and a download page, and says a prebuilt binary is available for some platforms through an SSL-protected download page. The project's own docs are split by major release (1.2.x, 1.3.x, 1.4.x). The binaries named in the package metadata are sockd and socksify. I did not check the configuration or download pages, so requirements beyond this are unknown.
brief.standout: Dante is a long-running, commercially backed open-source SOCKS server, and the homepage says it is used daily by Fortune 100 companies both as a forward proxy and as a reverse proxy. The docs index also collects an unusually full set of SOCKS-related standards and drafts, plus performance reports from production deployments.
brief.status: Maintained but slow-moving. The most recent release listed is Dante 1.4.4, dated 2024-12-15, and a security advisory followed on 2024-12-16. The roadmap on the homepage says it was updated September 2026 and lists 1.5.0 as planned for Q1 2027, with its status reverted from 'completed and in testing' to 'correction of problems discovered by new AI tools'. The footer reads copyright 1998-2025.
brief.caveats: The homepage says Dante 1.5.0 has slipped and is not yet released; the current stable line is 1.4.x. The license is described as BSD/CMU-type with complete source code included. Commercial support, customized installs, and several commercial modules are sold by the vendor, and some modules are paid. Prebuilt binaries exist only for some platforms. The 1.4.0 through 1.4.3 line has a security issue (CVE-2024-54662) in some configurations that use socksmethod in client rules, and a patch exists for 1.4.3; 1.4.4 includes the fix. The homepage states no outstanding security patches for 1.4.4. I did not verify any of these details beyond the homepage text.
quotes: It consists of a SOCKS server and a SOCKS client, implementing RFC 1928 and related standards.
Once installed, Dante can in most cases be made transparent to clients, providing functionality somewhat similar to what could be described as a non-transparent Layer 4 router.
Dante is used daily by Fortune 100 companies and large international organizations, both as a standard (forward) proxy server and as a reverse proxy server.
